subject: OKR stewardship: alignment notes, scope trims, and bridging asks for QBR prep
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: OKR stewardship: alignment notes, scope trims, and bridging asks for QBR prep

Team —

Quick mid-quarter check-in as I start drafting the leadership QBR narrative. High level: we are tracking toward the outcome but several workstreams need narrower scope or a short-term bridging plan to preserve velocity. I attached a one-page stewardship summary (QBR-stewardship-notes-v1.pdf) and a priority matrix (qbr-priority-matrix.xlsx).

Please read the bullets below and reply with commitments by EOD today. I want to capture promises in the QBR doc Friday morning.

Summary status
- Customer latency OKR: amber — baseline improvements done; tail latency reduction needs an integration milestone with the new routing policy.
- Cost/unit OKR: green — quantization trial ahead of schedule but needs a 2-week validation run.
- Platform reliability OKR: amber — rollback window for a canary must be tightened; ops dependency below.

Immediate asks (actionable asks per owner)
1) Vanessa: scope trim — can we reduce the tail-latency experiment matrix to the two highest-impact kernels for the QBR? If yes, confirm which two by 2pm.
2) Naomi: can you secure the Ops slot for the routing-policy integration (estimated 2 days, infra change window) next Tue-Wed? This is blocking tail-latency progress.
3) Marissa: please prepare a concise customer-facing note (one paragraph) that explains the planned canary behavior and fallback guarantees for the uptime SLA — I want to include it in the QBR. Draft due 3pm.

External coordination
- Elaine (Acme Analytics): I copied her as there's a critical dependency on their test harness for the validation run. Elaine — can you confirm availability week of Nov 9? If not, what alternative test windows do you have?
- Cloud marketplace partner: we may need a limited capacity bump during canary; I've flagged partners-success for a quick eligibility check.

Attachments:
- QBR-stewardship-notes-v1.pdf (pdf)
- qbr-priority-matrix.xlsx (xlsx)

Thanks — short replies appreciated so I can land the narrative.

Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwoodinference.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR stewardship: alignment notes, scope trims, and bridging asks for QBR prep

Markus —

I can trim the experiment matrix. Recommend we keep:
- Kernel B (large context attention opt) — highest impact on 95th pct
- Kernel D (kv-cache refactor) — best perf/cost tradeoff for our workloads

Rationale: both cover >70% of our p95 regressions and are independent enough to give a signal for QBR. I can cut Kernel A/C and rerun the smaller bench.

I'll commit to final configs by 14:00 PT. If Ops needs an extra preflight, flag it and I'll pause the bench start until it's green.

Vanessa
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: OKR stewardship: alignment notes, scope trims, and bridging asks for QBR prep

Markus / Vanessa / Marissa —

I reserved an Ops window for Tue-Wed (Nov 10-11) as requested; booking reference: OPS-7892. Two notes:
1) We need a short preflight checklist from Vanessa by EOD Mon so infra can stage the env and the rollback policy. Minimal items: change flags, expected traffic profile, and a failback runbook.
2) I flagged partners-success for a temporary capacity uplift; they asked for the projected peak qps and duration — Vanessa, can you post numbers to the Drive link? Partners asked that we share the expected peak within 24 hours to approve the bump.

I added the Ops slot to the shared calendar and updated the QBR doc with the timeline.

Naomi
Director, Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OKR stewardship: alignment notes, scope trims, and bridging asks for QBR prep

Thanks — short updates below and a draft paragraph for the QBR.

1) Customer note (for QBR):
"We will run a controlled canary that prioritizes availability. During the canary window, traffic will be routed to the new policy for a small percentage of requests; automatic fallback to the verified baseline is guaranteed on error rates above threshold. Customers will see no loss of profile data; observability and tracing remain intact. We expect the rollout to reduce 95th percentile latency within two weeks post-validation."

2) Partners/testing: Elaine, thanks for coordinating. If Acme can provide the harness week of Nov 9, that aligns with the Ops slot Naomi reserved. Can you confirm by EOD?

3) Attachments and artifacts: added the draft paragraph to the Drive folder and linked the QBR-stewardship-notes-v1.pdf. Also attached a one-line customer-facing FAQ for support teams.

I'll fold any edits into the final doc and stand by for the bench results.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
